 ET Online Diwali 2026 Lakshmi Puja Muhurat: Check city-wise puja timings for November 8, including Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, Bengaluru and other major cities.
 Diwali 2026 is being celebrated today, Sunday, November 8, with Lakshmi-Ganesh Puja forming the most important religious observance of the festival. Devotees across India worship Goddess Lakshmi and Lord Ganesha during the auspicious evening hours to seek wealth, prosperity, happiness and wisdom. Observed on Kartik Amavasya, If you are preparing for Diwali Puja today, knowing the correct Diwali Shubh Muhurat for Lakshmi Pujan is important.
 The auspicious timings vary across cities because of differences in local sunrise and sunset times. Here is a city-wise guide to Lakshmi Puja Muhurat 2026, along with Amavasya Tithi, Pradosh Kaal and other important Panchang details.

 Diwali 2026 Lakshmi Puja Muhurat: City-Wise Timings 
Lakshmi Puja is traditionally performed during Pradosh Kaal, the evening period after sunset. The Vrishabha Kaal, also known as Sthir Lagna, is considered particularly auspicious for worshipping Goddess Lakshmi. Here are the city-wise Lakshmi Puja timings for November 8, 2026. All timings are in Indian Standard Time (IST).

 Kolkata 5:20 PM – 7:18 PM 
 Patna 5:28 PM – 7:25 PM

 Diwali 2026: Important Panchang Timings
According to the New Delhi Panchang, Diwali falls on Kartik Amavasya. The following are the important timings for the festival:
 Panchang Details Date and Time 
 Diwali date Sunday, November 8, 2026 
 Amavasya Tithi begins November 8, 11:27 AM 
 Amavasya Tithi ends November 9, 12:31 PM 
 Pradosh Kaal 5:31 PM – 8:09 PM 
 Lakshmi Puja Muhurat 5:54 PM – 7:50 PM 
 Vrishabha Kaal 5:54 PM – 7:50 PM 
 Nishita Kaal 11:38 PM – 12:31 AM (November 9) 
 Also Read: Kartik Amavasya Date, Tithi Timings, Significance and Rituals 
 Why Is Lakshmi Puja Performed During Pradosh Kaal?
Pradosh Kaal is the period immediately after sunset and is considered auspicious for evening prayers and religious rituals. On Diwali, devotees worship Goddess Lakshmi during this period to seek her blessings for wealth, abundance, peace and prosperity.
The Vrishabha Lagna, which falls within the evening worship period, is considered favourable because Vrishabha is a fixed zodiac sign. According to Hindu religious traditions, performing Lakshmi Puja during Sthir Lagna is associated with stability and lasting prosperity.
